newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN POLICE RAID PIRATE CD SELLERS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN POLICE RAID PIRATE CD SELLERS.

text.p: Police in the Bulgarian capital on Tuesday raided vendors selling pirate compact discs and audio cassettes as part of a crackdown on the trade in which Bulgaria is second only to China.
An Interior Ministry statement said police confiscated more than 1,000 pirate CDs and 1,500 pirate audio cassettes.
Last month police checked CD producing firms in Sofia and in the towns of Botevgrad, Veliko Tarnovo and Stara Zagora, inspecting producers' lines and storage.

The interim government which took office in February vowed to crack down on audio-visual piracy and the interior ministry said on Wednesday police had seized more than 200,000 pirate CDs in the first four months of the year.
Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev will retain his post in the new cabinet to be voted by parliament on Wednesday.
Intellectual piracy has flourished in Bulgaria with the liberalisation of its markets since the fall of its communist rule in 1989.

The International Federation of Phonographic Industry (IFPI), representing a $40 billion international recording industry, said Bulgaria was producing an estimated 15 million discs a year and five CD plants were estimated to supply approximately one in eight of all illegal copies on the world CD blackmarket.
Washington put Bulgaria on a "watch list" last October and the IFPI urged the EU to block Bulgaria's accession to the World Trade Organisation until it cracked down on piracy.
